title_en: Mo Meihuan and Cen Runming v. Cen Rong'an, Cen Zhuo, and Lin Yuedi — inheritance dispute
keywords_en: civil; inheritance dispute; first instance; basic people's court; Guangdong Province; natural person; Marriage Law; Inheritance Law; determination of community property; proportion of estate division; determination of partnership operation facts; partial support; community property; contracting of hardware and wood furniture store; forged evidence; marriage; Lin Yuedi inheritance dispute
full_text_en:
Mo Meihuan and Cen Runming v. Cen Rong'an, Cen Zhuo, and Lin Yuedi — inheritance dispute

Plaintiff: Mo Meihuan, female, 28 years old, employee of a cooperative store in Guizhou Town, Shunde County, Guangdong Province. Residing at Heping Village, Guizhou Town.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Rongye, lawyer from Foshan Second Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Caiying, lawyer from Foshan Second Law Firm.

Plaintiff: Cen Runming, male, 5 years old.

Legal representative: Mo Meihuan, mother of Cen Runming.

Defendant: Cen Rong'an, male, 35 years old, self-employed worker.

Defendant: Cen Zhuo, male, 59 years old, farmer.

Defendant: Lin Yuedi, female, 56 years old, farmer. The above defendants currently reside at Heping Village, Guizhou Town, Shunde County, Guangdong Province.

Third party: Fang Changguang, male, 34 years old, employee of Xingfu Hardware Factory, Guizhou Town, Shunde County.

The People's Court of Shunde County, Guangdong Province, lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a public hearing in the case of the plaintiffs Mo Meihuan and Cen Runming v. the defendants Cen Rong'an, Cen Zhuo, and Lin Yuedi concerning an inheritance dispute.

Plaintiff Mo Meihuan alleged that the hardware and carpentry shop contracted by her husband Cen Hua'an during his lifetime, the telephone installed, and the two-story building constructed were property acquired during the continuance of their marriage, and she was entitled to the right to divide the jointly owned property and to inherit her husband's property. Cen Runming was the lawful heir of Cen Hua'an. The defendants now intended to misappropriate these properties. She requested protection of her and Cen Runming's lawful inheritance rights.

Defendant Cen Rong'an defended that the hardware and carpentry shop was a joint venture of four persons: Cen Zhuo contributed capital, Fang Changguang contributed the shop premises, Cen Hua'an was responsible for management, and he was responsible for sourcing goods, not a sole proprietorship of Cen Hua'an. The telephone was applied for and installed by him, and Cen Hua'an paid the fee on his behalf, which he had already repaid. For the two-story building where the plaintiff currently resided, Cen Hua'an contributed only 1,000 yuan, with most of the funds contributed by Cen Zhuo, Cen Rong'an, and others. Therefore, he requested protection of their lawful rights and interests.

To facilitate enforcement after judgment, the People's Court of Shunde County, upon the application of plaintiff Mo Meihuan and in accordance with Article 92, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), issued a ruling on February 11, 1987, for preservation of assets within the scope of the claims.

The People's Court of Shunde County found the following facts: Plaintiff Mo Meihuan is the sister-in-law of defendant Cen Rong'an and the daughter-in-law of defendants Cen Zhuo and Lin Yuedi. Mo Meihuan married Cen Hua'an, son of Cen Zhuo, in 1981, and gave birth to a son, Cen Runming, in 1982. In April 1983, Cen Hua'an, through Cen Rong'an, negotiated with his wife's brother-in-law, Fang Changguang (the third party in this case), and with the consent of the production team at that time, transferred the carpentry shop originally contracted by Fang Changguang and already out of business to Cen Hua'an. The shop was later renamed the Hardware and Carpentry Shop of the Tenth Production Team, Xingfu Village, and was operated solely by Cen Hua'an. Economic activities such as accounts, loans, payment of management fees, taxes, etc., were conducted in the name of Cen Hua'an. In the initial stages of operation, Cen Rong'an briefly assisted Cen Hua'an in sourcing goods, after which Cen Hua'an conducted purchases and sales on his own. During this period, as the hardware and carpentry shop was doing well and yielding substantial profits, Cen Hua'an and Mo Meihuan built a two-story building in Heping Village, purchased a television set, a washing machine, and other electrical appliances, a 125cc motorcycle, and installed one telephone for 1,900 yuan at Cen Rong'an's home. The shop operated by Mo Meihuan had remaining stock valued at 1,000 yuan. In March 1986, Cen Hua'an fell ill and entrusted Cen Rong'an to manage the hardware and carpentry shop. On April 30 of the same year, Cen Hua'an died of illness. In May of the same year, Mo Meihuan demanded to take over the hardware and carpentry shop left by her husband, but defendant Cen Rong'an refused to hand it over, giving rise to a dispute. In June of the same year, Mo Meihuan filed a lawsuit with the People's Court of Shunde County, requesting protection of her and Cen Runming's right to inherit Cen Hua'an's estate.

Regarding whether the hardware and carpentry shop was contracted and operated solely by Cen Hua'an or as a partnership, it was found that in June 1986, Cen Rong'an colluded with the third party, Fang Changguang, to forge a false contract to prove that the originally contracted carpentry shop was in fact a partnership operated by Cen Zhuo contributing capital, Fang Changguang contributing the shop premises, Cen Rong'an sourcing goods, and Cen Hua'an managing the shop. Cen Rong'an and others also colluded with insiders, telling them to "mind their own business." This proved that the hardware and carpentry shop was operated solely by Cen Hua'an and was not a joint venture.

The plaintiff's claims in the complaint to retrieve 15 pieces of fir timber that Cen Hua'an had left at the home of his younger brother, Cen Nan'an, in 1985, and to inherit Cen Hua'an's share of 160 pieces of fir timber jointly purchased by him and his family before marriage, as well as defendant Cen Rong'an's assertion that he had funded the installation of the telephone, were all unsupported by evidence and were not upheld.

During the trial, defendants Cen Rong'an and third party Fang Changguang forged evidence and fabricated a false contract. In accordance with Article 77 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), it was decided to impose a fine of 200 yuan on each and give them a reprimand and education.

During the proceedings, the People's Court of Shunde County entrusted the county timber company and other units to assess the value of the property in dispute, including the assets of the hardware and carpentry shop and the building where the plaintiff currently resided. The valuations were as follows: existing timber in the hardware and carpentry shop: 28,000 yuan; roof of the timber shed: 7,030 yuan; machinery and equipment in the shop: 800 yuan; one motorcycle: 3,815 yuan; one telephone set: 1,900 yuan; the building where the plaintiff currently resided: 33,392 yuan; television set, washing machine, etc., in the plaintiff's home: 1,900 yuan; remaining stock in the shop operated by Mo Meihuan: 1,000 yuan. The total amounted to 77,837 yuan.

After ascertaining the facts and distinguishing right from wrong, the People's Court of Shunde County attempted mediation but failed to reach an agreement.

The People's Court of Shunde County held that the hardware and carpentry shop, the telephone, and the two-story building where Mo Meihuan currently resided, which were the subjects of the dispute between plaintiff Mo Meihuan and defendants Cen Rong'an, Cen Zhuo, and Lin Yuedi, were property acquired during the continuance of the marriage between Mo Meihuan and her husband Cen Hua'an. Pursuant to Article 13, Paragraph 1 of the Marriage Law of the PRC, this property was jointly owned by the husband and wife. Pursuant to Article 26, Paragraph 1 of the Inheritance Law of the PRC, which provides that where property jointly acquired by husband and wife during the continuance of their marriage is to be partitioned as an inheritance, one half of the jointly owned property shall first be set aside for the spouse, and the remainder shall be the decedent's estate, the jointly owned property of Mo Meihuan and Cen Hua'an acquired during their marriage, totaling 77,837 yuan, was to be divided, with 38,918.5 yuan set aside for Mo Meihuan and the remaining 38,918.5 yuan constituting Cen Hua'an's estate. In accordance with the order of succession specified in Article 10, Paragraph 1 of the Inheritance Law of the PRC, Mo Meihuan, Cen Runming, Cen Zhuo, and Lin Yuedi were heirs of the first order. In accordance with Article 13, Paragraph 2 of the Inheritance Law of the PRC, heirs who have special financial difficulties and lack the capacity to work shall be given consideration in the distribution of the estate. Heirs Cen Zhuo and Lin Yuedi were currently contracting several dozen mu of fish ponds and were relatively well-off; Mo Meihuan was in the prime of life and had the capacity to work. These three could together inherit one quarter of Cen Hua'an's estate. Cen Runming was only five years old and lacked the capacity to work; he could inherit three quarters of the estate.

On May 19, 1987, the People's Court of Shunde County rendered the following judgment:

1. The hardware and carpentry shop, the two-story building where Mo Meihuan currently resided, the one telephone set installed at Cen Rong'an's home, the 125cc motorcycle, the remaining stock in the shop operated by Mo Meihuan, the television set, the washing machine, etc., valued at a total of 77,837 yuan, are jointly owned by plaintiff Mo Meihuan and Cen Hua'an, with each entitled to one half.

2. Of Cen Hua'an's estate of 38,918.5 yuan, Mo Meihuan, Cen Zhuo, and Lin Yuedi shall each inherit 3,243.21 yuan; Cen Runming shall inherit 29,188.87 yuan. The share inherited by Cen Runming shall be managed by his legal representative, Mo Meihuan.

3. The sum of 6,486.42 yuan inherited by Cen Zhuo and Lin Yuedi, of which 1,900 yuan shall be paid by Cen Rong'an (Cen Hua'an's telephone set shall belong to Cen Rong'an), and the remaining portion shall be paid by Mo Meihuan within 30 days after this judgment becomes legally effective.

Court acceptance fee of 778.37 yuan shall be borne by Cen Rong'an; the fee of 120 yuan for engaging relevant personnel to verify the assets of the hardware and carpentry shop, etc., shall be borne by Mo Meihuan.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, neither the plaintiffs nor the defendants appealed.
